text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Heads of municipalities earn less than corporate managers and top government officials, according to study by the local authorities' labour market institute.
- Finland's stagnating furniture industry wants to learn networking business principals from their Danish rivals.
- Government should openly debate NATO membership, says EU Minister Ole Norrback.
- Finnish vacuum-packed whitefish suspected to have caused three cases of severe food poisoning in Germany.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Forex market will be lively this week as Bank of Finland aims to keep markka from strengthening, Handelsbanken strategist Carlo Erakallio says. There is room to boost central bank reserves since 45 billion markka worth of foreign currency government debt will mature.
- Hardware sales are expected to stay on the fast growth track that started last summer.
- Cultor has cleared the unexpected raw materials problems which hit results early last year, finance director Filip Frankenhaeuser says.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- A large state debt is no problem for a welfare state, says economist John Kenneth Galbraith. He says financial markets have too much money and too little intelligence.
DEMARI
- Prime minister Paavo Lipponen says the Bank of Finland will not need support from other European central banks to keep the markka exchange rate stable.
- Tax cut should be directed at value-added tax since lower income taxes would just lead to tighter tax on consumption, says Terttu Malin, president of Finland's consumer association.
AAMULEHTI
- Kesko has been in talks on the sale of parts of Tuko and the strongest candidate is a group of former Tuko wholesalers, Kesko source says. Announcements are possible this week.
TURUN SANOMAT
- The people of Turku celebrated the centenary of Olympic legendary long distance runner Paavo Nurmi.
